domain: Interconnect and communication (on-die wires to AU-scale laser links), 2026-2300
summary: Interconnect from die to AU, 2026-2300. Invariants: 2 pF/cm wires (1/4CV^2), 3.336 us/km light (4.9 in glass), lambda/D diffraction, ~10 photons/bit uncoded. Wire energy only falls with V^2 (42 -> 9 fJ/bit/mm on-die); 3D bonding cuts die-to-die to ~2-30 fJ/bit; optical I/O falls 5.6 pJ (2026 product; 0.12 pJ lab) -> 0.4 (2040) -> 0.1 (2070) -> 0.03 pJ (2100+). Q1: photonic express lanes in the film (laid drawn-silica fibre or <=0.1 dB/m waveguides, continuous across 171 hinge folds) make a 279 m sail one tightly coupled 14.8 MW machine: mean global bit 2.2 pJ (2040) -> 0.11 (2070) -> 0.03 pJ (2100+) vs 440-1,465 pJ on the electrical mesh; sail-wide all-to-all 6e-5 / 3.3e-4 / 6.4e-4 B/FLOP at 10 % energy (NVLink-class), per-chiplet bandwidth flat in distance, MoE all-to-all 2-5 % of energy (2070-2100+) instead of 60-78 %; latency 0.9 us mean, 2.7 us worst (vs 11-94 us electrical); fabric 0.2-4 % of sail mass. Plausible ~2050-2070. Q2: light binds per-layer collectives beyond one sail (0.15-1.06 ms to neighbours; decode floor 38-271 ms), and inside a sail only costs batch (5e6-4e7 tokens for <=10 %). A 2070 sail runs a 1e28-class step at critical batch in ~0.6 s (1e28 FLOP in ~20 days); cross-sail DP is laser-bandwidth-bound (~100 Pbps per sail needed vs ~6), so the sail is the synchronous unit. Q3: a terminal carries ~50 / 200 / 400 Tbps (2040/2070/2100+) for 3.4 / 0.75 / 0.21 pJ/bit, spectrum-limited not photon-limited: 10 cm suffices to 330-360 km (all sail-sail neighbours), 30 cm to ~3,000-5,000 km (sail-pod); ~12 per sail (6-30) = 0.2-2.7 % of sail mass, <0.05 % of power; 2026-style 10 cm terminals would be 17-524 % of mass. Pod-pod km links are multi-beam (Pbps). Q4: interconnect-driven pod share 4 % -> 1.5 % -> 0.2 % -> 0; switching moves into the film (chiplet forwarding 0.75-7.5 Tb/s/site, non-volatile optical circuit switches), gateways are terminals with 0.1-0.3 m2 radiators, trunks are small relay craft (<1e-7 of swarm mass). Q5: hierarchical network, ~60-70 hops, 15-35 min light time (chords through the hollow interior 36 % shorter than along the shell); relays 1.6e-8 -> 1.4e-9 J/bit/AU, a byte across 1 AU stays ~1e7 FLOPs in every era. Synchronous cooperation: one sail (~3e-17 of the swarm); DiLoCo-class islands 1e2-1e5 sails; only hour-scale asynchronous syncs reach 97-99 % of the swarm (0.5-2.6 Tbps bisection).

architecture_implications.question: 1. With on-film optical waveguides at ~10-100 fJ/bit, does a 50-300 m sail behave like one tightly coupled machine? Does that remove the global-bandwidth penalty that made pods useful? When?
architecture_implications.answer: Yes for bandwidth and energy, from ~2050-2070; latency stays light-limited at ~1-3 us across the sail. Per-chiplet bandwidth becomes flat in distance instead of falling as 1/L.
architecture_implications.numbers: Per chiplet at 10 % of 0.14 W: electrical mesh 233 Gb/s at 2.5 cm but 0.2 Gb/s at 30 m and 0.021 Gb/s at 279 m (2070); photonic 197 Gb/s flat to 279 m (4.6e-04 B/FLOP), port-capped. Sail-wide uniform all-to-all at 10 % energy: electrical 8.2e-08 B/FLOP vs photonic 6.2e-05 (2040, gateway-access limited), 3.3e-04 (2070), 6.4e-04 (2100+) - above NVLink's 5e-5-1e-4. Mean global bit 2.2 / 0.11 / 0.03 pJ vs electrical 1,465 / 440 / 220 pJ (x658-7225). Layer-local MoE all-to-all: electrical 60-78 % of chip energy vs photonic 20 % (2040), 4.5 % (2070), 2.4 % (2100+). Latency: photonic 0.93 us mean, 2.75 us worst vs electrical 15-44 us mean/worst (2070). Needs loss <=0.1 dB/m (ULL SiN 0.034 demonstrated) or laid drawn-silica fibre (0.0003 dB/m), continuous across 171 hinge folds (jumper pairs would add 34-171 dB). Fabric mass for 1e-5 B/FLOP sail-wide: 0.2-1.2 % of sail; 1e-4: 2-4 % with ULL strips or 7-core fibre, 12 % with single-core fibre (2070). Plausible: express lanes ~2040-2050, chiplet-native receiverless ports (<=20 fJ) ~2060-2070.
architecture_implications.evidence_class: physics floor (light time, 2 pF/cm) + demonstrated lab (0.034 dB/m, 120 fJ/bit link, 0.9 fJ modulators) + speculation (film integration, era energies)

architecture_implications.question: 2. Does the speed of light become the binding constraint for synchronous work?
architecture_implications.answer: Inside a sail: only for per-layer collectives at small batch (it costs concurrency, not feasibility). Across sails: yes for every per-layer collective (TP, MoE); data- and pipeline-parallel across sails are laser-bandwidth-bound before they are latency-bound.
architecture_implications.numbers: Per-layer compute at batch 1 falls to ~3 ns in an 8 m patch (2070) and 0.003 ns for a whole sail. Batch for latency <=10 %: patch 90-440 tokens (photonic) vs 2,200-8,400 (electrical mesh); whole sail 5e6-4e7 tokens; neighbour sails 44-317 km 2e9-3e10 (impossible). Decode token floor from 2 collectives x 128 layers: patch 12-42 us, sail 0.70 ms, neighbour sails 38-271 ms. Training step at critical batch on ONE sail: 0.71 s (2040), 0.61 s (2070); a 1e28-FLOP run takes 20 days on one 2070 sail. DP all-reduce latency across 44-317 km is <=0.7 % of a step, but fully synchronous DP across 10 sails needs ~97 Pbps per sail (2070) vs ~6 Pbps of terminals. Pipeline across sails: 6e-8 B/FLOP per boundary = 2.7 Pbps per sail (2070), 4-28 micro-batches in flight hide 0.15-1 ms. Pod island (2 km): 6.7 us.
architecture_implications.evidence_class: physics floor (light time) + speculation (model shapes, critical batch 2e8 tokens in 2070)

architecture_implications.question: 3. Laser-link bandwidth by era for sail-sail, sail-pod, pod-pod; power and mass fraction; scaling with FLOP/s x8-250
architecture_implications.answer: Per terminal: ~50 Tbps (2040), ~200 Tbps (2070), ~400 Tbps (2100+), set by optical bandwidth x spectral efficiency, not photons: 10 cm suffices for every sail-sail neighbour (<=330-360 km), 30 cm for sail-pod/regional links to ~3,000-5,000 km; pod-pod inside km islands is unbounded in practice (hundreds to thousands of spatial modes). Terminals stay <3 % of sail mass and <0.05 % of sail power because 30 cm apertures and WDM grow faster than FLOP/s.
architecture_implications.numbers: Sail-sail 139 km: 9.6 / 50 / 200 / 400 Tbps per terminal at 39 / 3.4 / 0.75 / 0.21 pJ/bit. Sail-pod 3,000 km: 0.18 (10 cm, 2026) / 50 / 200 / 385 Tbps. Pod-pod 0.5-2 km: 0.06-0.15 Pbps (2026, 10 cm SDM) -> 3.2 / 51 / 410 Pbps aggregate with 64-1024 parallel beams. Need per sail = beta_ext x 8 x FLOP/s: service traffic (1e-8 B/FLOP, the 2026 design rule) 15 -> 118 -> 455 -> 845 Tbps; low-comm training (1e-7) 0.15 -> 1.2 -> 4.5 -> 8.4 Pbps. Terminals: 6 (service) to 27-30 (training) x 9-13 kg = 0.4-2.7 % of sail mass, 0.2-4.8 kW = 0.001-0.03 % of power. Keeping 2026 tech (10 cm, 9.6 Tbps cap) at FLOP/s x8/30/56/250 would need 480-15,000 terminals = 17-524 % of sail mass; 30 cm: 9-284 terminals = 0.8-25 %.
architecture_implications.evidence_class: physics floor (diffraction, Friis) + demonstrated (9.6 Tbps design, 402 Tb/s per mode in fibre) + speculation (era DSP energy)

architecture_implications.question: 4. What pod share is still justified by interconnect (switching, global shuffles, gateways)? Should switching become a film function?
architecture_implications.answer: ~4 % today -> ~1.5 % (2040, hedge) -> ~0.2 % (2070) -> 0 (2100+). Yes: switching moves into the film (distributed electrical forwarding in chiplets, non-volatile optical circuit switches and passive wavelength routing on the lanes); gateways are just laser terminals with 0.1-0.3 m2 radiators; trunk relays are separate small craft.
architecture_implications.numbers: A 0.15 W site switches 30-75 Gb/s (2026) -> 150-500 Gb/s (2040) -> 0.75-3 Tb/s (2070) -> 3-7.5 Tb/s (2100+); 1 % of a sail's sites = 2e+18 b/s of switching (2070). Film photonic global bit vs 3-tier pod fabric: 2.2 vs 3.5 pJ (2040), 0.11 vs 0.8 pJ (2070), 0.03 vs 0.24 pJ (2100+). Gateway heat per 30 cm terminal 85-170 W -> 0.07-0.14 m2 at 330 K. Trunk relay craft (6 x 1 m terminals, ~0.5 t) on a 48,000-160,000 km lattice: 4e8-6e10 craft = 2e-12-5e-8 of swarm mass. Combined with study 2: pods fall to ~5 % (2040), ~1 % (2070), ~0.3 % (2100+), all memory/archive/cryogenic driven.
architecture_implications.evidence_class: speculation (switch energy by era) + demonstrated (OCS <3 % of TPU v4 power; PCM zero static power)

architecture_implications.question: 5. Swarm-scale networking: topology, hops, latency; what fraction can cooperate synchronously?
architecture_implications.answer: Hierarchical laser network: in-sail photonic fabric; 6-12 persistent links per sail to co-moving ring neighbours (44-317 km); 30 cm long-range links (1e3-1e4 km); 1-3 m trunk relays (5e4-1.6e5 km hops); 3 m photon-counting chords through the empty interior. ~60-70 hops end to end, <1 ms processing on top of 15-35 min light time. Synchronous cooperation is capped at one sail (~3e-17 of the swarm at f=0.01); low-communication training reaches ~1e2-1e5 sails; only asynchronous, hour-scale outer syncs span the swarm.
architecture_implications.numbers: Light time: chord 918 s (0.92 AU) to 1,347 s (1.35 AU); along the shell 1,442-2,116 s. Neighbour-mesh-only routing: 2e6-1.5e7 hops, 1-150 s of processing and 0.4-590 uJ/bit - unusable; hierarchy: 60-70 hops. Energy per bit per AU (1 m relays): 1.1e-7 -> 1.6e-8 -> 3.9e-9 -> 1.4e-9 J; direct 3 m photon-counting chord at 1 AU: 77-230 Gbps at 1.4-4.3 nJ/bit (100 W). A byte across 1 AU stays ~1e6-1e8 FLOP-equivalents in every era. Self-occultation: sun-facing sails give each shell crossing tau = -ln(1-f): 1 / 10 / 50 % of radial lines blocked at f = 0.01 / 0.1 / 0.5; tangential links see sails edge-on. Link lifetimes: co-moving ring neighbours 0.01-0.1 m/s -> 770-1,300 h; crossing rings 1 km/s -> 0.7-5 min (acquisition 22-34 s costs 10-70 %). Sails within latency radius: 3 us -> 1 sail; 1 ms -> 1 (f=0.01) to 228 (f=0.5); 50 ms -> 7.5e4-2.9e7; 900 s -> 97-99 %. Bandwidth caps fully synchronous DP at 1 sail; DiLoCo-class (1e3x less traffic) 230-1,070 sails; 1e5x less 2e4-1e5 sails. Swarm-wide hourly reduce of a 1e28-class model needs only 0.5-2.6 Tbps of bisection.
architecture_implications.evidence_class: physics floor (light time, occultation geometry) + speculation (algorithms, orbit plan)

architecture_implications.question: On-film photonics engineering: layers, coupling, bends, hinges, mass and Mercury manufacturability
architecture_implications.answer: Pattern lanes, do not blanket the film; use two lane layers (x and y) that cross vertically; carry long lanes in drawn Mercury-silica fibre that survives the hinge folds; keep deposited waveguides for <=1-10 m local lanes.
architecture_implications.numbers: Blanket waveguide layers would cost 0.018 (8 um SiN/Al2O3 stack), 0.046 (ULL SiN, 21 um) or 0.066 kg/m2 (PLC, 30 um) each = 8-32 % of the 0.207 kg/m2 sail; lanes need only 0.1-18 % of area per axis at 1e-5-1e-4 B/FLOP (0.1-4 % with 7-core fibre or ULL strips), so 2 lane layers suffice and 2-4 is the practical maximum before the laminate-moment (<=3 K-equivalent) and IR-emitter stack are disturbed. A y-lane crosses 93-279 x-lanes (1-3 m spacing): in-plane crossings at 0.12-0.17 dB would add 11-47 dB, interlayer crossings at 0.001 dB add 0.1-0.3 dB. Taps: evanescent/interlayer couplers 0.1-0.4 dB at the tapping chiplet, ~0.005-0.01 dB per pass-by, so each waveguide serves <=~200 taps; splitters 0.1-0.3 dB. Bends: ULL SiN ~12 mm, PLC 2-5 mm, fibre 5-10 mm - direction changes happen by O-E-O at a chiplet or by interlayer couplers, not in-plane bends. Hinges: 171 fold lines per side at ~8 mm fold radius; fibre strain 0.5 % (80 um) - 0.8 % (125 um) is below the ~1 % proof test, a 21 um deposited stack at 0.13 % is at thin-film flaw strength (~100 MPa) and would crack; jumper pairs would add 34-171 dB. Materials: SiO2 (abundant) purified by chlorination (Cl detected by MESSENGER), Ti (1e20-3e20 kg) or Ge (5e15-5e16 kg) core dopant, no hydrogen so no OH absorption; Al2O3 (Al abundant); Si3N4 needs ~1e-7 kg N per m2 (Mercury N unmeasured; ppm suffices); 1550 nm lasers need In (1e14-1e15 kg inventory) at mg per sail, or switch to 9xx nm GaAs sources with Si/Ge detectors (+0.8 dB/km Rayleigh is irrelevant at 300 m). ULL SiN needs ~1000 C thermal oxide: make it (and fibre) off-film as ribbons and laminate.
architecture_implications.evidence_class: demonstrated lab result (losses, crossings, fibre bend specs) + speculation (film integration)

architecture_implications.question: Placement rule that follows
architecture_implications.answer: Make the sail the unit of synchronous work and the unit of networking: one sail = one ~15 MW scale-up domain (1-3 us), sails group into DiLoCo islands of 1e2-1e5 within ~1,000-30,000 km, the swarm cooperates only asynchronously. Pods lose their interconnect role; the remaining pod fraction is set by memory (study 2) and any cryogenic logic (study 1).
architecture_implications.numbers: Sail synchronous unit 14.8 MW; island 1.5-1,500 GW; swarm 5e23-3.4e25 W.

Consolidate to ~12 terminals (6-30): ~8 small 10 cm neighbour terminals (as today's, but no longer one per patch) at boom tips and hub, plus ~4 larger 30 cm long-range terminals on the hub/service plates; no per-patch masts.

wildcards.wildcard: Low-staleness training at 1e6+ islands (asynchronous methods that tolerate 15-35 min of light time)
wildcards.effect: Turns the swarm's 97-99 % asynchronous reach into one useful training job; bisection need is only Tbps; the binding limit is algorithmic.

wildcards.wildcard: Film-wide optical phased arrays (the sail's own back face as a conformal 1-10 m aperture)
wildcards.effect: 10-100x range or rate at sail spacing with no discrete terminals; needs closed-loop phase control over a membrane flat only to ~mm.

wildcards.effect: n_g 1.003: sail-scale collectives 32 % faster (1.33 us diagonal), lower nonlinearity; heavier (~200 um OD).

wildcards.wildcard: Free-space optics across the back of the sail (mast-to-mast micro-terminals)
wildcards.effect: Vacuum light speed and no hinge crossings; limited by membrane flatness, shadowing and pointing.

wildcards.effect: AU-scale direct chords 10-100x faster at fixed power; matters only for Earth/long-haul since those bits are already <1e-4 of swarm energy.

wildcards.wildcard: On-film optical amplification without erbium (semiconductor or Raman)
wildcards.effect: Lets lossy deposited glass (1-10 dB/m) span the sail; removes the ULL/fibre requirement.

wildcards.wildcard: Fully passive wavelength-routed all-to-all (AWGR-like) at sail scale with thousands of wavelengths
wildcards.effect: No O-E-O turn: one optical hop any-to-any, ~2x lower energy and <1 us mean latency.
